categories.main_business_segments: Halliburton operates through two main business segments: Completion and Production, and Drilling and Evaluation. The Completion and Production segment provides cementing, stimulation, specialty chemicals, intervention, pressure control, artificial lift, and completion products and services. The Drilling and Evaluation segment offers field and reservoir modeling, drilling, fluids, evaluation, and precise wellbore placement solutions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Halliburton leverages advanced technologies such as digital and automation platforms, cloud-based software, artificial intelligence, and intelligent drilling and completion systems. The company manufactures most of its own equipment and invests in R&D for hydraulic fracturing, electric fracturing systems (Zeus), intelligent rotary steerable systems (iCruise), and environmentally friendly chemical solutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Halliburton's primary customers are major, national, and independent oil and natural gas producers worldwide. The company serves the upstream energy sector, supporting customers throughout the lifecycle of oil and gas reservoirs, from exploration and drilling to completion and production optimization.
categories.geographic_coverage: Halliburton operates in more than 70 countries, with business organized around four primary geographic regions: North America, Latin America, Europe/Africa/CIS, and Middle East/Asia. In 2023, 44% of revenue was from the United States, with significant operations and growth in the Middle East/Asia and Latin America.
categories.supply_chain_position: Halliburton is positioned as a diversified energy services provider, primarily serving the upstream segment of the oil and gas supply chain. The company delivers products and services that support exploration, drilling, well construction, completion, and production activities.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include international growth, digital and automation technology deployment, capital efficiency, and sustainability. Halliburton is focused on advancing clean energy solutions, reducing emissions, participating in carbon capture and storage, and supporting the energy mix transition through Halliburton Labs and R&D in decarbonization technologies.
categories.revenue_model: Halliburton generates revenue primarily through the sale of services and products to the energy industry, including project-based service contracts, product sales, and software licensing. Most contracts are short-term, with some long-term integrated project management and digital/software agreements.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Halliburton is one of the world's largest diversified energy services companies, competing with other major oilfield services firms such as Schlumberger and Baker Hughes. The company maintains a leading market position through technical differentiation, global reach, and a broad portfolio of services and products.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Halliburton reported $23.0 billion in revenue, a 13% increase over 2022, with operating income of $4.1 billion. The company demonstrated strong international growth (17% increase in international revenue), robust cash flows, and a commitment to shareholder returns, including $1.4 billion returned via buybacks and dividends.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Halliburton emphasizes collaboration and engineering solutions to maximize asset value for customers, focusing on improving efficiency, increasing recovery, and maximizing production. The company differentiates itself through technical innovation, digital integration, capital efficiency, and a commitment to sustainability and the energy transition.
